findings.source_passage: Oh, sweet friends! hearken to me. It was made of small juicy clams, scarcely bigger than hazel nuts
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'But when that smoking chowder came in'
findings.why_it_matters: The apostrophe 'Oh, sweet friends! hearken to me' is one of the most recognizable voice-establishing rhetorical moments in the chapter, signaling Ishmael's mock-epic register and the comic elevation of ordinary food into sublime experience; its absence erases this tonal peak entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Oh, sweet friends! hearken to me' verbatim before the chowder description; the hazel-nut simile should also be reinstated as it is part of the signature phrasing.

findings.source_passage: thinks I to myself, I wonder now if this here has any effect on the head? What's that stultifying saying about chowder-headed people?
findings.why_it_matters: This digressive aside—with its self-conscious comic musing and the phrase 'chowder-headed people'—is a characteristic Ishmael voice moment, blending folk idiom with mock-philosophical speculation; its complete absence removes both voice texture and the eel joke that follows.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'chowder-headed people' musing and the 'live eel in your bowl / Where's your harpoon?' line, which together form a short but tonally signature comic exchange.

findings.source_passage: but that's a rather cold and clammy reception in the winter time, ain't it, Mrs. Hussey?
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'What's that about Cods, ma'am?'
findings.why_it_matters: Ishmael's 'cold and clammy reception' pun is a signature piece of his playful low humor and is the clearest joke in the scene; dropping it flattens the comedic exchange with Mrs. Hussey to bare transaction.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'cold and clammy reception in the winter time' line verbatim or near-verbatim inside the dialogue exchange with Mrs. Hussey.

findings.source_passage: there was a fishy flavor to the milk, too, which I could not at all account for, till one morning happening to take a stroll along the beach
findings.source_locator: final descriptive paragraph about the Try Pots
findings.why_it_matters: The draft compresses 'fishy milk' and the brindled cow episode but strips Melville's deadpan build-up ('which I could not at all account for, till…') that makes the absurdist payoff land; 'looking very slip-shod, I assure ye' is also dropped, losing Ishmael's characteristic self-deprecating tag.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain 'looking very slip-shod, I assure ye' and the narrative build ('which I could not at all account for, till one morning') to preserve the comic rhythm of the anecdote.

summary: The draft's single most damaging failure is the erasure of 'Oh, sweet friends! hearken to me'—a high-severity signature loss—compounded by the removal of the 'chowder-headed' digression, the 'cold and clammy reception' pun, and the 'slip-shod, I assure ye' tag, all of which together gut the chapter's characteristic Ishmaelean comic voice.
